summary:
China will strengthen World Bank cooperation, prioritising knowledge work under the new Country Partnership Framework for China. 
The finance ministry said the partnership will aid China’s high-quality development and support developing countries’ common prosperity. 
Loans to China have gradually declined as national strength improved, reflecting changing domestic demand and a shift in cooperation.

title: World Bank approves $150 mn for Sri Lanka's REGROW reforms
summary:
The World Bank has approved $150 million financing for Sri Lanka’s REGROW policy operation, the first in a proposed three-part series. 
The reforms target lower trade barriers, a better investment climate, and stronger competitiveness, relevant for exporters and sourcing teams. 
Budget support also covers financial-sector, state-owned enterprise, power-sector, and women’s employment measures.

summary:

title: India extends zero customs duty on PTA, MEG till July 15
summary:
India has extended the zero customs duty on PTA and MEG imports until July 15, 2026, providing temporary relief to polyester producers amid West Asia-related supply disruptions.
The move is expected to ease raw material costs, though downstream polyester prices may take longer to normalise due to high-cost inventories and uneven pass-through.

title: India’s technical textile exports triple in a decade
summary:
India’s technical textile exports have more than tripled over the past decade to ₹28,392 crore in FY25, driven by government support and rising Sportech demand, Minister Pabitra Margherita said.
At the Sportech Bharat Vision 2047 conference, industry urged duty and GST reforms, while officials highlighted NTTM’s focus on commercialisation and innovation.

title: US declines USMCA renewal in its current form
summary:
The United States has not agreed to renew USMCA in its current form after a July 1, 2026 joint review with Mexico and Canada.
The pact remains in force while the parties seek to resolve issues, keeping North American trade arrangements operational for importers and sourcing teams.
US-Mexico bilateral talks are scheduled for the week of July 20.

title: Italian textile machinery eyes revival through innovation
summary:
Italy's textile machinery production fell 9 per cent and exports declined 8 per cent in 2025 amid weak global demand, but India emerged as the largest export market with sales rising 28 per cent to €176 million. 
ACIMIT said innovation, sustainability, digitalisation and talent development will be central to strengthening competitiveness ahead of ITMA 2027.

title: ICE cotton continues to rise on third day, supported by gains
summary:
ICE cotton futures rose for a third straight session, with the December 2026 contract settling at 77.84 cents, supported by gains in Chicago grain markets.
However, larger-than-expected US cotton acreage and weaker crude oil prices limited the rally.
Traders now await the US Department of Agriculture’s weekly export sales report for fresh demand signals.

title: UK manufacturing upturn shows signs of losing momentum in June
summary:
The upturn in UK manufacturing showed signs of losing momentum at the end of Q2 2026, S&P Global said. 
The PMI signalled expansion in each of the past eight months. 
Output, new orders and employment expanded and suppliers' delivery times lengthened. 
New work inflows improved for the seventh month in a row in June, and the month saw new export business rise for the sixth month in a row, but mildly.

title: Italian-Irish venture to set up footwear factory in Bangladesh
summary:
Italian and Irish-backed Deltaport Footwear will invest $21.6 million to set up a footwear factory at the Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority Economic Zone in Mirsharai, Chattogram.
The unit will have an annual production capacity of around 3 million pairs.
The factory is expected to create 468 jobs and generate annual export earnings of about $37.5 million.

title: South Korean apparel imports up 1% to $4.8 bn in January-May 2026
summary:
South Korea's apparel imports rose 1 per cent year on year to $4.806 billion during January-May 2026, driven by higher knitted apparel imports and a stronger May performance.
However, exports of man-made filaments and knitted fabrics declined amid weak global textile demand and intensifying competition from lower-cost producers worldwide.

title: EU apparel imports reach $205.6 bn amid supplier squeeze
summary:
Europe has become the global battleground for apparel sourcing as more suppliers compete for slower import growth.
Rising volumes, falling unit prices, tighter compliance rules and stronger buyer leverage are squeezing margins.
Future competitiveness will depend less on low prices and more on speed, traceability, product mix and value-added manufacturing.

title: US’ Nike reports stable FY26 revenue amid market headwinds
summary:
Nike has reported flat FY26 revenue of $46.4 billion as North American growth offset weaker demand in China and EMEA. 
Wholesale sales increased, while Nike Direct and Converse declined. 
Despite lower annual profit, the company advanced its long-term growth strategy. 
In Q4, revenue dipped 1 per cent, but tariff recovery sharply lifted gross margin, net income, and earnings per share.

title: UK backs Philippines' path towards CPTPP accession
summary:
CPTPP parties will begin preparatory discussions with the Philippines, Indonesia, and the UAE after a virtual commission meeting recently. 
For apparel and textile exporters, any future Philippine accession could mean lower tariffs, simpler rules, and stronger supply-chain links. 
The talks do not guarantee accession or formal negotiations.

title: Türkiye's apparel exports fall 4.6% in Jan-May amid weak global demand
summary:
Türkiye's apparel exports fell 4.59 per cent year on year to $6.464 billion in January-May 2026 as weak demand continued to weigh on shipments.
The slowdown deepened in May, when exports dropped 13.85 per cent after April's brief recovery, amid cautious global buying, smaller orders, and rising competition from lower-cost sourcing destinations.

title: Turkiye’s $6.6 bn apparel exports chase new markets
summary:
Turkiye’s apparel exports show a strategic shift rather than a simple slowdown. 
Weak EU demand is being partly offset by growth in the Middle East, Eastern Europe, Africa and the Americas, but newer markets may not match Europe’s margins.  
Sustained growth will depend on leveraging textile integration, faster lead times, compliance and higher-value, design-led apparel.
